chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu al-Maghra', from al-Halbi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who bought a sheep, kept it for three days, then returned it: He (peace be upon him) said: 'If during those three days he drank its milk, he should return it along with three amdad (handfuls of grain); and if there was no milk for it, there is nothing upon him.'

key_terms.أَمْدَادٍ: Handfuls (plural of mudd, a unit of volume)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on returning a purchased animal after drinking its milk?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* establishes the principle of *dam* (compensation) for the consumption of an animal's milk during a three-day retention period, reflecting the Shia juristic focus on fair exchange in commercial transactions. The specific measure of 'three handfuls' (amdād) highlights the practical application of customary market standards in determining liability, ensuring the seller is made whole for the value lost. It underscores the ethical imperative of not depriving the owner of their property's utility when returning goods.
